The real network behavior exposes actual latency and error patterns, letting us test the interface against real conditions—not approximations. The trade-off is burning dev hours on infrastructure that might change, but we avoid the bigger cost of debugging fake responses when real data behaves differently.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A thin stub with mocked latency and errors still risks hiding the real failure modes—network timeouts, partial payloads, or rate-limiting—until we hit them in production. The real risk isn’t dev hours; it’s shipping an interface that works in the lab but fails under real load. Settle it: run the real endpoint behind the flag for one night, log the failures, then decide tomorrow if the cost was worth the data.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship a thin live API stub tonight with mocked responses to test the interface against realistic conditions without extensive infrastructure commitment; Pane owns this delivery.
